title: Pythia: Compiler-Guided Defense Against Non-Control Data Attacks
problem: Modern C/C++ applications are vulnerable to Non-Control Data Attacks, particularly Control-flow Bending where adversaries manipulate program data to flip branch outcomes and divert control flow. Existing CFI mechanisms fail to defend against such attacks involving branch predicate manipulation.
motivation: Protecting applications from sophisticated non-control data attacks that bypass current state-of-the-art defenses is critical for system security.
method: Pythia uses compiler-guided techniques to defend against control-flow bending attacks by protecting branch predicates from data corruption. The compiler instruments programs to detect and prevent unauthorized data modifications that would affect branch decisions, extending beyond traditional control-flow integrity approaches.
key_novelty: Compiler-guided defense mechanism that specifically targets control-flow bending attacks by protecting branch predicates from non-control data manipulation.
contributions: Identifies limitations of CFI mechanisms against control-flow bending attacks
Proposes compiler-guided defense for protecting branch predicates
Addresses non-control data attacks that alter control flow through data corruption
Extends defense beyond traditional control-flow integrity
